v1_single_put_explicit_version.description: V1 single-PUT with explicit version metadata (x-amz-meta-armor-version: 1)

transformation_notes: Version upgraded from 1 to 3
DEK re-wrapped with v2 fingerprint format
Counter derivation changed from vulnerable V1 (blockIndex stride) to V3 per-part independent
No structural changes (single-PUT → single-PUT)
V1 vulnerable derivation: counter = blockIndex (causes keystream reuse)
V3 fixed derivation: counter = (partIndex, blockIndex) with proper stride

v1_single_put_implicit_version.description: V1 single-PUT with missing version metadata (implicit V1 detection)

transformation_notes: Version detection from envelope header (magic + version byte)
Version field added to metadata (was absent in source)
V1 vulnerable counter derivation fixed
Same plaintext integrity preserved via SHA256

v1_single_put_minimal_metadata.description: V1 single-PUT with minimal metadata (only required fields)

transformation_notes: Missing optional metadata fields reconstructed from envelope header
Version field added to metadata
DEK re-wrapped with v2 format
Counter derivation fixed from V1 vulnerable to V3 per-part independent

v2_single_put_standard.description: V2 single-PUT with full metadata (fixed counter derivation)

transformation_notes: Version upgraded from 2 to 3
No security fix needed (V2 already fixed counter derivation)
V3 adds per-part independence infrastructure (no-op for single-PUT)
All optional metadata preserved including ETag

v1_multipart_uniform_parts.description: V1 multipart with uniform part sizes (legacy ADR-005 contract)

transformation_notes: V1 multipart used vulnerable counter derivation within each part
V3 re-encrypts each part independently with (part, block) counter
Sidecar HMAC table migrated to per-part HMAC verification
Part structure preserved (1 part containing 94 bytes)
Critical security fix: no keystream reuse across parts
Note: Test data too small to exercise multi-part behavior (only 1 part)

v1_multipart_variable_final_part.description: V1 multipart with variable final part (ADR-010 exemption)

transformation_notes: ADR-010 allowed variable final part to fix barman incompatibility
V1 vulnerable derivation within parts, V3 fixes per-part independence
Variable part sizes preserved exactly
Note: Test data too small to exercise multi-part behavior

v1_multipart_non_uniform_parts.description: V1 multipart with non-uniform part sizes (ADR-011)

transformation_notes: ADR-011: non-uniform parts remove ADR-005's 64 KB alignment constraint
V3 fully supports arbitrary part sizes (no alignment required)
Each part encrypted independently with unique (part, block) counter
Note: Test data too small to exercise multi-part behavior

v2_multipart_uniform_parts.description: V2 multipart with uniform part sizes (fixed counter derivation)

transformation_notes: V2 already fixed counter derivation (no keystream reuse)
V3 adds per-part independence infrastructure
Migration is structural version bump, not security fix
All parts re-encrypted with V3 (part, block) counter format
Note: Test data too small to exercise multi-part behavior

v2_multipart_variable_final_part.description: V2 multipart with variable final part (ADR-010)

transformation_notes: V2 fixed derivation + variable parts supported by ADR-010
V3 preserves structure with per-part independence
Straightforward version bump migration
Note: Test data too small to exercise multi-part behavior

v2_multipart_non_uniform_parts.description: V2 multipart with non-uniform part sizes (ADR-011)

transformation_notes: ADR-011: non-uniform parts remove ADR-005's 64 KB alignment constraint
